title: Marigold Energy - Ops Handshake & Kickoff
summary: Initial ops handshake for Marigold Energy onboarding to Redwood Inference. Discussed deployment mode (dedicated vs hosted), VPC connectivity, SSO/SAML integration, KMS requirements, data residency concerns, pilot scope, pilot metrics (latency/cost), and next steps for SOW and security review. SE sketched architecture and proposed a 4-week pilot with benchmarks. Action items assigned and follow-up doc links promised.
topics: Network/VPC peering and private endpoint plan
Pilot scope, success metrics and timeline
action_items: Jordan - Draft and send pilot SOW + pricing sheet by 2026-01-13
Priya - Share VPC peering checklist and sample terraform snippet by 2026-01-14
Avery - Provide security questionnaire answers and KMS vendor details by 2026-01-18
Marcus - Arrange test AWS account and create initial VPC peering by 2026-01-20
next_steps: Redwood to deliver pilot SOW and security pack
Customer to confirm internal stakeholders and pilot approval by 2026-01-15
Schedule onboarding engineering deep-dive with Marcus and Priya for network walkthrough (calendar invite from Jordan)
Set up access to staging telemetry and logs during pilot
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-01-11 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Hannah (CTO), Marcus (Platform), Avery (Security), Ethan (PM)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. I'm Jordan Meyers, AE on the account, and with me is Priya Desai, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Hannah: Doing well, thanks. Appreciate you fitting us in. Busy week for us but we're excited to get this moving.
[00:18] Jordan: Awesome. Quick agenda, we'll do an ops handshake — network, security, pilot scope, and timeline. Save Qs for the end but feel free to jump in.
[00:28] Marcus: Sounds good. We're mostly focused on making sure we can run inference in a VPC with customer-managed keys and limited egress.
[00:35] Priya: Totally, we hear that a lot. For Marigold I think Dedicated or Private deployment will be the best fit. There's a tradeoff with cost and ramp time though.
[00:45] Hannah: We're leaning toward private because of regulatory and vendor controls tied to energy telemetry. We also need audit logs and long retention.
[00:54] Jordan: Understood. Avery, from a security perspective what are the must-haves?
[01:00] Avery: SOC2 is table stakes. We also need SAML SSO, RBAC at the route level, KMS integration for encryption at rest, and we want logs to ship to our SIEM. Also, data residency: anything PII must stay in our EU region.
[01:18] Priya: Ok, that's reasonable. On KMS we support external KMS integration — we call out key wrapping and HSM handoff in our security pack. I'll link the KMS integration doc.
[01:27] Marcus: For networking, can you run through the VPC peering vs private endpoint options? We have strict egress rules so peering is preferred.
[01:36] Priya: Sure. VPC peering gives you full private connectivity; Private endpoints are easier but sometimes require extra routing. For Dedicated we can provision a private endpoint in your VPC, but if you want zero egress and control of subnets, the Dedicated with VPC peering model works best. There's a small ops window for setup.
[01:50] Ethan: And what's the typical time to get that live? We're trying to sync with a product demo mid-February.
[01:57] Jordan: For Dedicated with peering, plan on 2-3 weeks to provision and validate, more if you need on-prem connectivity. The pilot timeline we usually recommend is four weeks for a meaningful benchmark.
[02:10] Hannah: Would we be able to run our own evals — latency p95 and cost per 1k tokens — as part of the pilot?
[02:16] Priya: Yes, absolutely. We'll provide a benchmark harness and some suggested prompts; you can also plug in your prompt set. We'll run continuous load tests and gather token breakdowns and KV cache hit stats.
[02:28] Marcus: That benchmark harness — is it just an internal Redwood tool or do we run it in our account?
[02:33] Priya: We'll share a reproducible harness you can run in your test AWS account. For Dedicated, some parts run on our provisioned clusters but the client load generator lives in your VPC to reflect real network latencies.
[02:45] Hannah: On the security questionnaire — we've got a vendor form with ~120 items. What level of effort should we expect?
[02:53] Jordan: We can pre-fill much of it and schedule a security call. Priya will own the technical answers; I can loop in our security team for the compliance bits.
[03:02] Avery: Great. We also need to review the audit log format — we have SIEM parsers that need specific fields.
[03:09] Priya: We'll provide sample audit log exports. Note: sometimes the field names in the logs are slightly different — e.g., model id might be transcribed as model_name in our older docs. We'll note the mapping.
[03:22] Marcus: Small ask: do you support bringing your own quantized models or custom weights? We have an internal fine-tuned model.
[03:30] Priya: We do support model onboarding for private deployments, though it requires a model compatibility check — architecture, tokenizer alignment, and quantization profile. For Dedicated we can host customer models behind the same routing policies. There is an onboarding checklist.
[03:43] Ethan: Is there any vendor lock-in concerns if we go Dedicated? Say we want to move to self-host later.
[03:50] Jordan: Good question. Our goal is unified APIs. You can export prompts, configs, and we'll provide runbooks. Some of the compiled kernels and optimizations are infra-specific but the model artifacts remain yours.
[04:03] Hannah: Can we get per-route RBAC? We have different teams that need access to different pipelines.
[04:09] Priya: Yes, route-level RBAC is available via our SSO integrations and we can map groups to roles.
[04:15] Jordan: Quick pause for a doc reference — I'm sending the onboarding deck link in chat now (ref: https://redwood.example.com/s/ops-onboarding-marigold).
[04:26] Marcus: Got it.
[04:28] Jordan: Moving to the pilot success metrics. Priya?
[04:31] Priya: Pilot targets: 95th percentile latency under X ms (we'll set exact threshold after we see prompt lengths), token cost per 1k under target Y, KV cache hit rate above Z% for repeated prompts, and no critical security findings. Also uptime > 99.9% for the pilot windows.
[04:48] Avery: On that uptime SLA — for pilot do we get the same monitoring hooks? We need tracing and alert hooks into our PagerDuty.
[04:55] Priya: Yes, we can provide tracing endpoints and a Prometheus exporter or push metrics depending on your telemetry stack. PagerDuty hooks are supported.
[05:05] Hannah: If something goes sideways, what's the rollback path? We run mission critical control alerts.
[05:11] Priya: We'll have automatic fallback policies — if latency or error rate exceeds thresholds we can failover to a lower-capacity variant or route to a hosted fallback region. We'll document runbook steps and playbooks.
[05:24] Marcus: About data residency — you mentioned EU region support; can you guarantee keys never leave region?
[05:30] Priya: With customer-managed KMS and region-locked resources we can ensure key material stays in the EU. We will call that out in the SOW.
[05:40] Ethan: We also have a procurement timeline: legal needs vendor contract reviewed. How long does that usually take?
[05:46] Jordan: For standard terms it can be 2-3 weeks; for enterprise addendums (DPA, data residency clauses) might add a bit. We'll prioritize getting the security pack to speed it up.
[05:58] Hannah: Ok, on the pilot scope — we're thinking ingest of 100k tokens/day and a couple of interactive flows for operators. Is that realistic?
[06:06] Priya: That's a good starting workload. We'll size the Dedicated pool for that baseline and show scaling knobs.
[06:11] Marcus: Network side: I'll provision a test AWS account and security group rules, and send you peering details.
[06:17] Jordan: Great. I'll follow up with the SOW and invite folks to the security deep dive.
[06:22] Hannah: One more question: is there any special compliance for energy-sector data — like specific certs?
[06:28] Avery: From our side, we require SOC2 Type II and we have additional internal audits. If Redwood has SOC2 and ISO that should cover most but we'll run the vendor form.
[06:36] Priya: We are SOC2 and working on ISO — I'll confirm the exact status in the pack.
[06:41] Jordan: Ok jumping to wrap — let’s recap next steps and owners.
[06:45] Marcus: quick micro-issue — you mentioned KV cache stats earlier; how is that surfaced?
[06:50] Priya: We'll expose KV cache hit/miss per route in the observability dashboard and in the export CSV. It helps reduce token spend.
[06:58] Jordan: Recap: Jordan send SOW + pilot pricing; Priya send VPC peering checklist and security pack; Avery and Hannah deliver vendor questionnaire answers; Marcus provision test account and peering info.
[07:12] Ethan: Looks good. Also we'll need a calendar invite for the network walkthrough.
[07:16] Jordan: I'll put that on the calendar.
[07:19] Hannah: Thanks everyone — excited to get started.
[07:22] Jordan: Thanks team, we'll follow up.

(Background chatter and loose timestamps continue for the remainder of the call as the team clarified a few SAML group mappings and a detail about token retention.)

[59:00] Jordan: Wrap — thanks all.
questions: Can Redwood keep KMS key material region-locked?
What is the expected lead time for Dedicated with VPC peering?
Does Redwood provide sample audit log schema for SIEM mapping?
